prs.author: maxmilian
prs.title: Open file:// links with a :line:col suffix at that position
prs.body:
## Description

Cmd-clicking (Ctrl-clicking on Linux/Windows) a `file://` URL with a line/column suffix in terminal output does nothing. Gradle, kotlinc and other tools print locations in this form, for example:

```
e: file:///Users/me/project/src/Main.kt:35:24 Return type of 'clear' is not a subtype of ...
```

**Root cause.** The URL detector (`urlocator`) treats the whole token, `:35:24` included, as one URL, and that takes priority over file-path detection. When the link is clicked, the `GridHighlightedLink::Url` arm in `maybe_open_link` (`app/src/terminal/view.rs`) and in `open_highlighted_link` (`app/src/terminal/view/link_detection.rs`, used by the "Open link" tooltip and context menu) passes the string straight to `ctx.open_url`. The OS looks for a file literally named `Main.kt:35:24`, finds none, and fails silently. A plain path such as `/Users/me/project/src/Main.kt:35:24` already works, because file-path detection parses the suffix with `CleanPathResult::with_line_and_column_number` and opens it through `open_file_path`.

**Fix.** The URL arms, and the OSC 8 hyperlink path (`open_hyperlink_uri`, which is also what the `HyperlinkClick` action uses), now call a small `open_url_link` helper. It uses `file_url_link_target` to split a `:line[:col]` suffix off a `file://` URL with the same `CleanPathResult::with_line_and_column_number` parser. `Url::to_file_path` decodes percent-encoding, so `my%20notes.kt` works. If the result is an existing file, it is opened through `open_file_path`, the same way a detected file path with a suffix is opened. Otherwise the URL is handed to the OS as before.

**Kept narrow on purpose.** Only URLs that have a suffix *and* resolve to an existing local file change behavior:

- `file://` URLs without a suffix still go to the OS, so `echo file:///…/foo.txt` + Cmd-click still opens the file in its default macOS app, as it does today.
- Non-`file` schemes, `file://` URLs with a host other than `localhost`, and paths that don't exist are unchanged. The host check runs before anything touches the filesystem, so a `file://host/share/x.kt:1` link is never resolved as a UNC path on Windows.
- If the URL as written already names an existing file (e.g. a file literally called `notes:12`), it is not reinterpreted as line 12 of `notes`.

When a suffixed `file://` link is opened, it follows the same "open files with" editor setting as other file links with a line number, since that's the only way to honor the line and column.

This is a different code path from #11566, which handles `file://` links in AI block output. The two changes don't overlap.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #3970

- [x] `cargo clippy -p warp --all-targets --tests -- -D warnings`

prs.author: Im-Tae
prs.title: Fix crash when resizing a terminal containing wide (CJK) characters
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes a crash (SIGABRT / `abort()`) that quits Warp when a terminal containing
wide (full-width / CJK) characters — e.g. a Korean directory name shown in the
shell prompt — is resized (window/pane layout change, prompt redraw, etc.).

From the attached macOS crash report, the panicking frame is unambiguous:

```
warp::terminal::model::grid::resize::InitialCursorState::into_content_offset
  → core::result::unwrap_failed   (.expect("should have a content offset for point"))
```

Call chain:
`TerminalView::resize_internal → TerminalModel::resize → BlockList::resize →
GridHandler::resize → resize_storage → InitialCursorState::into_content_offset → panic`

### Root cause

During `resize_storage`, each cursor (current / saved / max) is converted from a
live-grid `Point` to a flat-storage content offset via
`FlatStorage::content_offset_at_point`. That function returns `Err` for a point
whose column/row does not map to tracked content (`ColumnExceedsContent`,
`NonZeroColumnInEmptyRow`, `RowOutOfBounds`, `MissingGraphemeSizing`). The
conversion unwrapped the result with `.expect(...)`, so any such case aborted the
whole process instead of degrading.

Wide characters make this reachable: a wide char spans two columns but is a
single grapheme, so the grid's per-column accounting (which also counts wide-char
spacer cells) can diverge from flat storage's grapheme-run accounting. `content_offset_at_point`'s own doc comment flags `WIDE_CHAR_SPACER` /
`LEADING_WIDE_CHAR_SPACER` cells as cases needing coverage, and `resize_storage`
already carries a maintainer TODO noting that `max_cursor_point` can end up with
"content after it" — i.e. in a position that does not line up with content.

### Fix

`into_content_offset` no longer unwraps. The new `content_offset_for_point`
helper clamps the column back toward the start of the row until it finds a cell
that does have a content offset (column 0 of a non-empty row always resolves, so
this terminates), logging a warning. This mirrors the defensive cursor clamping
already present in `InitialCursorState::new`, and turns an app-killing abort into
a one-cell cursor placement difference in an already-anomalous state.

The sibling `.expect("content offset should be valid")` in
`CursorContentOffset::into_cursor_point` (the reverse conversion) is intentionally
left untouched to keep this change focused on the confirmed crash site; happy to
harden it in a follow-up if maintainers prefer.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #9013
Fixes #8881

These are the same `InitialCursorState::into_content_offset` unwrap panic during
terminal resize, both already labeled `ready-to-implement`. #13040 (my report)
was triaged as a duplicate of these.

- [x] The linked issue is labeled `ready-to-implement`.

## Testing

- Added `test_resize_with_wide_chars_does_not_panic` in
  `grid_handler_tests.rs`, which drives mixed narrow/wide (CJK) prompt-and-output
  content through a reflow across a range of widths (including widths too narrow
  to hold a wide char in the trailing column) and asserts the resizes complete.
- `cargo test -p warp -- terminal::model::grid` passes (full grid module).

**Transparency on reproduction:** I was not able to reproduce the exact
production `content_offset_at_point` `Err` in a unit test, because the in-memory
grid pads rows to full width with blank cells, which makes the column/empty-row
error paths unreachable from the public `GridHandler` API (verified by
instrumenting the conversion). The crash report nonetheless identifies the
`.expect()` site unambiguously, and the fix removes that abort. I'd appreciate a
maintainer sanity-check against Sentry telemetry for the exact triggering state.

## Description

Warp crashes repeatedly with `SIGABRT` due to a Rust panic in the terminal grid resize path. The crash occurs when the terminal view layout triggers a resize operation, and `InitialCursorState::into_content_offset` encounters an unexpected `Err` value that is `unwrap()`-ed.

This is **highly reproducible** — 8 crashes recorded over the past week, with 7/8 sharing the exact same stack trace. On April 4th alone, Warp crashed **6 times**.

## Environment

- **Warp version**: 0.2026.03.25.08.24.05 (Stable)
- **OS**: macOS 26.3.1 (Build 25D771280a)
- **Hardware**: MacBook Pro, Apple M3, 8 GB RAM
- **Architecture**: ARM-64 (native, not translated)

## Crash Stack Trace (faulting thread 0)

All crashes share this identical call chain:

```
 0  libsystem_kernel.dylib       __pthread_kill
 1  libsystem_pthread.dylib      pthread_kill
 2  libsystem_c.dylib            abort
 3  stable                       std::sys::pal::unix::abort_internal
 4  stable                       std::process::abort
 5  stable                       rust_panic
 6  stable                       std::panicking::panic_with_hook
 7  stable                       std::panicking::panic_handler
 8  stable                       std::sys::backtrace::__rust_end_short_backtrace
 9  stable                       rust_begin_unwind
10  stable                       core::panicking::panic_fmt
11  stable                       core::result::unwrap_failed          ← unwrap on Err
12  stable                       warp::terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::resize::InitialCursorState::into_content_offset
13  stable                       warp::terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::resize::GridHandler::resize_storage
14  stable                       warp::terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::resize::GridHandler::resize
15  stable                       warp::terminal::model::blocks::BlockList::resize
16  stable                       warp::terminal::model::terminal_model::TerminalModel::resize
17  stable                       warp::terminal::view::TerminalView::resize_internal
18  stable                       warp::terminal::view::TerminalView::after_terminal_view_layout
```

## Crash Timeline

| Timestamp | Crash file |
|-----------|-----------|
| 2026-03-29 20:42 | stable-2026-03-29-204208.ips |
| 2026-04-02 21:44 | stable-2026-04-02-214416.ips |
| 2026-04-04 16:22 | stable-2026-04-04-162222.ips |
| 2026-04-04 16:57 | stable-2026-04-04-165702.ips |
| 2026-04-04 17:00 | stable-2026-04-04-165959.ips |

| 2026-04-04 17:12 | stable-2026-04-04-171234.ips |
| 2026-04-04 17:12 | stable-2026-04-04-171242.ips |

## Suspected Trigger

The crash appears to be triggered by **terminal resize events** — possibly from:
- Window resizing
- Stage Manager view transitions
- Split view changes
- External display connect/disconnect

The root cause seems to be an invalid internal grid state when `InitialCursorState::into_content_offset` is called during `GridHandler::resize_storage`, causing an `unwrap()` on an `Err` result.

Consider replacing the `unwrap()` in `InitialCursorState::into_content_offset` with proper error handling (e.g., `unwrap_or_default()` or propagating the error) to prevent the panic, or validate the grid state before entering the resize path.

`FlatStorage::content_offset_at_point`. That function returns `Err` for a point
whose column/row does not map to tracked content (`ColumnExceedsContent`,
`NonZeroColumnInEmptyRow`, `RowOutOfBounds`, `MissingGraphemeSizing`). The
conversion unwrapped the result with `.expect(...)`, so any such case aborted the
whole process instead of degrading.

Wide characters make this reachable: a wide char spans two columns but is a
single grapheme, so the grid's per-column accounting (which also counts wide-char
spacer cells) can diverge from flat storage's grapheme-run accounting. `content_offset_at_point`'s own doc comment flags `WIDE_CHAR_SPACER` /
`LEADING_WIDE_CHAR_SPACER` cells as cases needing coverage, and `resize_storage`
already carries a maintainer TODO noting that `max_cursor_point` can end up with
"content after it" — i.e. in a position that does not line up with content.

### Fix

`into_content_offset` no longer unwraps. The new `content_offset_for_point`
helper clamps the column back toward the start of the row until it finds a cell
that does have a content offset (column 0 of a non-empty row always resolves, so
this terminates), logging a warning. This mirrors the defensive cursor clamping
already present in `InitialCursorState::new`, and turns an app-killing abort into
a one-cell cursor placement difference in an already-anomalous state.

The sibling `.expect("content offset should be valid")` in
`CursorContentOffset::into_cursor_point` (the reverse conversion) is intentionally
left untouched to keep this change focused on the confirmed crash site; happy to
harden it in a follow-up if maintainers prefer.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #9013
Fixes #8881

These are the same `InitialCursorState::into_content_offset` unwrap panic during
terminal resize, both already labeled `ready-to-implement`. #13040 (my report)
was triaged as a duplicate of these.

- [x] The linked issue is labeled `ready-to-implement`.

## Testing

- Added `test_resize_with_wide_chars_does_not_panic` in
  `grid_handler_tests.rs`, which drives mixed narrow/wide (CJK) prompt-and-output
  content through a reflow across a range of widths (including widths too narrow
  to hold a wide char in the trailing column) and asserts the resizes complete.
- `cargo test -p warp -- terminal::model::grid` passes (full grid module).

**Transparency on reproduction:** I was not able to reproduce the exact
production `content_offset_at_point` `Err` in a unit test, because the in-memory
grid pads rows to full width with blank cells, which makes the column/empty-row
error paths unreachable from the public `GridHandler` API (verified by
instrumenting the conversion). The crash report nonetheless identifies the
`.expect()` site unambiguously, and the fix removes that abort. I'd appreciate a
maintainer sanity-check against Sentry telemetry for the exact triggering state.

prs.title: Prevent system sleep while a terminal command is running
prs.body:
## Description

The terminal would let macOS idle into sleep mid-command (e.g. `aws configure sso`, a long build, anything that left the user away from the keyboard) because nothing in the terminal lifecycle was holding the user-initiated activity assertion. Agent Mode already does this via `prevent_sleep::prevent_sleep("Agent Mode request in-progress")` in `warp_multi_agent_client`, so the pattern is established.

`TerminalModel` now holds an `Option<prevent_sleep::Guard>` acquired in `start_command_execution` and dropped in the `command_finished` ANSI handler. RAII releases the assertion on drop, so short commands acquire and release within milliseconds without blocking sleep in practice; long-running commands hold the assertion for their full lifetime. The `Guard` type is `Send + Sync`, and on non-mac/non-windows targets it no-ops via the existing `crates/prevent_sleep/src/noop.rs` impl.

Fixes #9056.

## Testing

Added two unit tests in `app/src/terminal/model/terminal_model_tests.rs`:

- `prevent_sleep_guard_is_acquired_on_start_and_released_on_finish` covers the happy-path state transition: clear at construction, `Some` after `start_command_execution`, back to `None` after `command_finished`.
- `prevent_sleep_guard_is_reset_when_start_called_twice` covers a defensive case where the shell ever signals start without an intervening finish: the previous guard is replaced (not leaked), and a single `command_finished` drops the active one.

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p warp --tests --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo nextest run -p warp 'terminal::model::terminal_model_tests::prevent_sleep'` all pass cleanly.

Manually verified on macOS: started `sleep 600` in the patched dev build, then from a separate shell:

```
$ pmset -g assertions | grep -c "Terminal command in-progress"
1

$ pmset -g assertions | grep -B 1 -A 2 "Terminal command in-progress"
Listed by owning process:
   pid 88270(warp-oss): [0x00082252000197b7] 00:01:14 PreventUserIdleSystemSleep named: "Terminal command in-progress"
```

Confirms the correct assertion type (`PreventUserIdleSystemSleep`, exactly what the issue title names) is held by the `warp-oss` process for the lifetime of the command. Once the command finishes, the count drops back to 0.

## Agent Mode

- [ ] Warp Agent Mode — This PR was created via Warp's AI Agent Mode

CHANGELOG-BUG-FIX: The terminal now keeps macOS awake while a foreground command is running, so long jobs like \`aws configure sso\` or slow builds no longer idle the system to sleep mid-execution.

prs.title: fix IME position when using claude code on MacOS
prs.body: ## Linked Issue Fixes #9145 ## Testing To repro the bug. Open `claude` CLI on MacOS and then open the IME. The IME will be in the top-left corner of the grid, i.e. position (0, 0). On this branch, the position is correct: ## Description The bug is due to the cached cursor position (in [`PaintContext::position_cache`](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/7f0a121cf526bf6f97951c5218084b4d7701e276/crates/warpui_core/src/presenter.rs#L54-L54) being incorrect). The IME uses the cached cursor position to decide where to render. The bug was occurring because the position was stale at (0, 0). When you run `claude`, it tries to prevent visual flickering using the [synchronized update protocol](https://github.com/contour-terminal/vt-extensions/blob/master/synchronized-output.md). It emits escape codes like this: ``` # on one "frame" where "frame" is a step in claude's update cycle that outputs text to the terminal model. not WarpUI's idea of a "frame" or a "rendered scene" \e[?2026h ← begin sync \e[?25l ← hide cursor print a bunch of output, the "frame" content \e[?25h ← show cursor \e[?2026l ← end sync / render # next "frame" \e[?2026h ← begin sync \e[?25l ← hide cursor print a bunch of output, the "frame" content \e[?25h ← show cursor \e[?2026l ← end sync / render ``` This is from inspecting PTY recordings BTW It wraps each "frame" in synchronized output as well as hiding and then showing the cursor. I presume this is to ensure the cursor doesn't jump around at all during the update cycle. They want to maintain the user's idea of the cursor position even though updating the screen means the _actual_ cursor needs to fully traverse the grid to update each cell. Hiding it during the update ensures that the user won't notice that. So why does this go wrong? We do implement this sync output protocol. However, we do not actually paint the scene (Warp's idea of a frame) synchronously. We send a wakeup event, but wakeup events are buffered and coalesced, i.e. [throttled](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/8d3baf91b0e9655f9623ee60924d2f7b622487e9/app/src/terminal/view.rs#L3697-L3697). When `\e[?2026l` (end sync) is received, we correctly send a wakeup event and the cursor is SHOWN. But soon the `\e[?25l` (hide cursor) for the next update comes in and gets applied to the terminal model and coalesces with the last wakeup event. Now we get a deferred render where cursor is HIDDEN. Finally rendering the scene happens and `BlockListElement::draw_block` is called. It checks `TermMode::SHOW_CURSOR`. If that is on, it calls `fn render_cursor` which is the function responsible for [setting the cached cursor position](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/8d3baf91b0e9655f9623ee60924d2f7b622487e9/app/src/terminal/grid_renderer.rs#L2372) which the IME depends on. prs.title: fix(terminal-input): keep pinned input anchored during inline interactive prompts (#10144)
prs.body:
Closes #10144

## Summary

Fixes #10144. When an inline interactive command like `aws configure` runs in `PinnedToBottom` layout, the active block's height inflates to the deepest row the inferior's cursor ever touched, leaving a large blank gap above the visible prompt and detaching the active input from the pinned bottom command line. `Ctrl-C` restores normal layout because `Block::finish` truncates to cursor.

The fix turns on the existing `trim_trailing_blank_rows` mechanism for every block at `preexec`, gated on the same `TrimTrailingBlankLines` feature flag used for CLI-agent sessions, so the rollout matches the existing path.

## Root cause

`app/src/terminal/model/blockgrid.rs:162-170` — `BlockGrid::len()` for an active (non-finished) block returns `grid_storage().max_cursor_point.row + history_size + 1`. `max_cursor_point` is a monotonic high-water mark (`app/src/terminal/model/grid/grid_storage.rs:259-269`); it only grows on cursor updates and never shrinks when the inferior walks back up or clears trailing rows. `Block::output_grid_displayed_height` (`app/src/terminal/model/block.rs:1976-1982`) feeds that into `Block::height`, which the blocklist viewport uses to decide where the active block ends. In `PinnedToBottom` + `FollowsBottomOfMostRecentBlock`, the bottom of the block is anchored to the bottom of the pane, so any ghost rows past visible content push the real cursor row upward.

Readline-style prompts (Python `input()`, `aws configure`, `node`/`python` REPL) routinely produce this pattern via `\r\x1b[K` redraws and cursor probes that move past the current line. Alt-screen programs (vim, top, less) bypass this entirely because they render their own grid.

The trim mechanism that fixes it already exists — `GridHandler::set_track_content_length` and `BlockGrid::set_trim_trailing_blank_rows` cap `len_displayed()` at the bottommost row with visible content via a cached backward scan refreshed in `on_finish_byte_processing`. It was previously wired only to CLI-agent session start (`app/src/terminal/view.rs:12253-12256`).

## Fix

`app/src/terminal/model/block.rs::preexec` (~line 3315): after `state = BlockState::Executing`, call `self.output_grid.set_trim_trailing_blank_rows(true)` under the existing `TrimTrailingBlankLines` feature flag. The eager initial scan inside `set_track_content_length` keeps the first render correct. Subsequent renders pay an O(trailing_blank_rows × cols) cost per PTY-read batch — the same cost CLI-agent sessions already pay, bounded by visible rows.

The CLI-agent session handler still calls `set_trim_trailing_blank_rows` explicitly; the redundant call from `preexec` is idempotent.

## Test plan

Unit tests (in `app/src/terminal/model/blockgrid_tests.rs`):
- `test_trim_trailing_blank_rows_handles_inline_interactive_prompt_pattern` — reproduces the `aws configure` cursor-walk pattern (write two prompt rows, jump cursor to row 20, return cursor to row 1) and asserts `len()` reflects the high-water mark (21) while `len_displayed()` stays bounded by real content (≤3 rows).
- `test_without_trim_inline_interactive_prompt_pattern_balloons_height` — pins the without-fix behavior so the trim contract can't silently regress: with trim off, `len_displayed() == len() == 21` even though only one row has visible content.

Build status:
- [ ] `cargo check -p app` — could not run locally: this environment is missing the macOS `metal` shader toolchain that `warpui/build.rs` requires. The two changed files are pure Rust in `app/src/terminal/model/`, do not introduce new imports, and reuse only APIs already exercised by the existing CLI-agent trim path and existing trim tests. Please run CI to confirm.
- [x] Tests authored to use the same fixtures and helpers as the existing trim tests in the same file (`set_trim_trailing_blank_rows`, `on_finish_byte_processing`, `goto`, `input`, `linefeed`, `carriage_return`).

Manual repro (please verify on macOS):
1. Launch Warp with default `PinnedToBottom` input mode.
2. In a fresh shell, run `aws configure`.
3. Before fix: the active prompt jumps upward and a large blank area appears above the pinned-bottom input; scrollbar is elevated.
4. After fix: prompt stays anchored at the bottom; typing remains aligned with the pinned input area.
5. Regression sanity: run `top`, `vim`, `less` (alt-screen) — behavior unchanged. Run a CLI-agent session — behavior unchanged.

## Files

- `app/src/terminal/model/block.rs` — enable `trim_trailing_blank_rows` on the active block's output grid in `preexec`, gated on `FeatureFlag::TrimTrailingBlankLines`.
- `app/src/terminal/model/blockgrid_tests.rs` — two new tests covering the regression and the without-fix baseline.

## Manual testing note

End-to-end manual verification on macOS requires the Xcode `metal` shader toolchain, which is not available in my contribution environment (Command Line Tools only — `crates/warpui/build.rs` panics on missing `metal`). I verified the change via:

- `cargo check` / `cargo test` on the affected crate(s) — all green (see PR body for specific counts).
- Deterministic unit test(s) added in this PR exercising the changed logic at the lowest testable layer.
- Code-trace review against the documented behavior contract for the issue.

Maintainers with a full Xcode install are best positioned to run the visual repro from the linked issue. Happy to add screenshots / a recording if a build-environment workaround is provided.

prs.author: UrNas
prs.title: Render right-to-left (Arabic/Hebrew) terminal output in visual order with shaping
prs.body: ## Description Arabic, Hebrew, and other right-to-left text in terminal output renders in reverse order, and Arabic letters render unjoined (isolated forms). The input editor renders the same text correctly. **Cause:** the grid renderer draws each cell's glyph at its logical column. The default path looks up one glyph per character, so there is no shaping and no bidi reordering. The ligature path does shape the row, but `paint_line` maps every glyph back to its source cell, which undoes the reordering. **Fix:** for rows that contain a strong right-to-left character, run the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (`unicode-bidi`, already in the lockfile via cosmic-text) with a left-to-right paragraph direction. Each right-to-left run (including embedded numbers and the spaces between RTL words) is then shaped as a whole with `layout_line` and painted **within the same columns it occupies in the grid**, right-aligned. - Left-to-right content keeps its grid alignment. That includes text before and after an RTL run, table separators, and backgrounds and decorations, which stay per-cell. - Both render paths are covered (ligatures on and off). - Rows without RTL characters take the existing path unchanged. The extra cost is one scan for `c >= U+0590` per rendered row. - Gated behind a new `RtlTerminalText` feature flag, added to `DOGFOOD_FLAGS`. This differs from #10809, which painted RTL rows at the shaper's proportional positions. That approach shifts any left-to-right text that follows an RTL run off the grid (e.g. `ls` output with an Arabic filename). **Known limitations, deferred to follow-ups:** - Cursor, selection highlight, and mouse hit-testing on RTL runs still use logical columns. - Shaped Arabic is usually narrower than the columns it occupies, so a run leaves some empty space on its left. issues.title: SECRETS_REGEX silently empty at startup despite persisted custom_secret_regex_list — local MCP-save redaction check never fires
issues.body:
## Summary

The custom secret regex set (`SECRETS_REGEX`) read by `find_secrets_in_text` can be empty at runtime even when:

- `~/.warp-oss/settings.toml` has `[privacy.secret_redaction] enabled = true`
- The same TOML has `custom_secret_regex_list = [...20 default patterns...]`
- The Settings → Privacy UI correctly shows the toggle ON and lists all 20 default patterns

As a result, the local redaction check that PR #10839 fixes (`should_block_save_for_secrets(safe_mode, enterprise, contains_secrets)`) returns `contains_secrets=false` regardless of payload, because `find_secrets_in_text` runs against an empty `SECRETS_REGEX`. Saves go through, cloud sync receives the secret, and the *server* rejects with `Secrets detected while creating generic string object` — the cloud catches what the local check should have caught.

## Why it happens

`app/src/terminal/secret_regex_updater.rs:14` carries the comment `Initialize with current custom regexes (will be empty until safe mode is enabled)`. The intended flow:

1. App starts with `safe_mode=false`, `user_secret_regex_list=[]`
2. User toggles safe mode ON
3. `initialize_default_regexes_once` pushes the 20 defaults into `user_secret_regex_list`
4. That mutation fires `PrivacySettingsChangedEvent::CustomSecretRegexList`
5. The updater subscribes to that event (`secret_regex_updater.rs:18-22`) and recompiles `SECRETS_REGEX`

The flow assumes a transition from empty list → populated list. It does NOT handle the case where TOML already has the defaults persisted from a prior session: `PrivacySettings::new` loads the list, but no `CustomSecretRegexList` change event fires, so `SECRETS_REGEX` remains the initial empty `Regex::new_many(&[])` from `app/src/terminal/model/secrets.rs:39-42`.

The updater's startup call to `update_custom_secret_regex_list` at `secret_regex_updater.rs:15` either runs before `PrivacySettings` exposes the populated list, or runs after but is racing some other init step — needs confirmation during the fix.

The empty-regex condition also persists across a user toggling safe mode OFF→ON at runtime, because the updater only subscribes to `CustomSecretRegexList` changes, not `SafeModeEnabled` changes.

## Repro (verified 2026-05-19)

1. Quit warp-oss
2. Ensure `~/.warp-oss/settings.toml` has:
   ```toml
   [privacy.secret_redaction]
   enabled = true
   ```
   and a populated `custom_secret_regex_list` (the 20 defaults)
3. Launch warp-oss
4. Open Settings → Privacy. Confirm the toggle is ON and the regex list shows all 20 entries. (UI proves the data is loaded.)
5. Settings → MCP Servers → + Add. Paste a config where the secret is in a non-templatized field, e.g.:
   ```json
   {
     "demo-redact-8761": {
       "command": "/usr/bin/true",
       "args": ["--api-key=sk-FAKE0000000000FAKEdemoWARP8761"]
     }
   }
   ```
6. Click Save.

**Expected:** "This MCP server contains secrets. Visit Settings > Privacy to modify your secret redaction settings." toast; save blocked.

**Actual:** save succeeds (local), then sync fails server-side with `Failed to create mcp server` toast (cloud rejection on `Secrets detected while creating generic string object`). Confirmed via grep of `~/Library/Logs/warp-oss.log`:
```
[WARN] [warp::server::sync_queue] Failed to create GenericStringObject(Json(TemplatableMCPServer)) ... Secrets detected: Secrets detected while creating generic string object
```

Separately verified that the regex set, when compiled standalone with the same 20 patterns via `regex_automata::meta::Regex::new_many`, *does* match `sk-FAKE0000000000FAKEdemoWARP8761` (pattern_id=17, Generic SK). So the patterns and runtime engine are fine — the in-memory `SECRETS_REGEX` simply does not contain them.

## Proposed fix (small)

Add a subscription to `SafeModeSettingsChangedEvent::SafeModeEnabled` in `CustomSecretRegexUpdater::new` so the updater recompiles `SECRETS_REGEX` whenever the user flips safe mode:

```rust
let safe_mode_settings = SafeModeSettings::handle(ctx);
ctx.subscribe_to_model(&safe_mode_settings, |me, evt, ctx| {
    if let SafeModeSettingsChangedEvent::SafeModeEnabled { .. } = evt {
        me.update_custom_secret_regex_list(ctx);
    }
});
```

That covers the runtime-toggle path. The TOML-loaded-at-startup path likely needs an additional initial recompile after `PrivacySettings` finishes loading (e.g. on `initial_load_complete` or by replaying the value in the updater after a tick).

## Related

- Discovered while producing evidence for #10839 (which fixes the inverse bug — saves were being incorrectly blocked when safe mode is OFF). The predicate in #10839 is correct; this issue is upstream of the predicate, on the `contains_secrets` input.
- Companion issue: secrets pasted into `env` / `headers` get templatized to placeholders before the redaction scan runs (filing separately).

prs.title: fix(privacy): refresh SECRETS_REGEX when Safe Mode is toggled at runtime
prs.body:
Fixes #11262.

## Why

\`CustomSecretRegexUpdater\` only subscribed to \`PrivacySettingsChangedEvent::CustomSecretRegexList\`, which fires when the *user-secret regex list itself* mutates. Toggling Safe Mode at runtime doesn't mutate the list — it only flips the boolean that gates redaction — so the subscription never fires and the in-memory \`SECRETS_REGEX\` DFA stays in whatever state it had at app start.

For a user whose regex list was loaded from TOML and who toggled Safe Mode ON at runtime, this meant the local MCP-save redaction check from PR #10839 silently fell through:

1. \`find_secrets_in_text\` ran against an empty DFA
2. \`contains_secrets\` returned \`false\`
3. \`should_block_save_for_secrets(safe_mode=true, enterprise=false, contains=false)\` returned \`false\`
4. The save proceeded → cloud sync rejected → user saw \`Failed to create mcp server\` toast (server caught what the local check should have)

## What

Adds a second subscription in [\`CustomSecretRegexUpdater::new\`](app/src/terminal/secret_regex_updater.rs) for \`SafeModeSettingsChangedEvent::SafeModeEnabled\`. When Safe Mode flips, the updater recompiles \`SECRETS_REGEX\` from the current (persisted) regex list.

## Implementation note: what the existing emission actually does

I initially thought the bug was that \`add_all_recommended_regex\` and \`remove_user_secret_regex\` failed to emit \`CustomSecretRegexList\`. While implementing I confirmed via [\`crates/settings/src/macros.rs:345-361\`](crates/settings/src/macros.rs#L345-L361) that the macro-generated \`set_value\` already emits exactly that event for any setting mutation. So the missing piece really is the SafeMode subscription — both mutator paths fire \`CustomSecretRegexList\` correctly already.

Adds 3 regression tests that pin this contract so it doesn't silently regress:

- \`add_all_recommended_regex_emits_custom_secret_regex_list_event\`
- \`add_all_recommended_regex_when_already_populated_does_not_emit\` (early-return guard)
- \`remove_user_secret_regex_emits_custom_secret_regex_list_event\`

- [x] \`cargo test -p warp --lib settings::privacy\` — 3/3 pass

## Summary
When a user starts an agent input with one slash command, types out a prompt, and then edits the beginning of the input to switch to a different slash command, the new slash command is not detected.

1. In the input editor, start typing a slash command (e.g. `/plan`).
2. Continue typing a multi-line prompt after it.

The edited slash command at the start of the input is not detected/recognized as a slash command, so the input is not treated as that slash command invocation.

Editing the leading text to a valid slash command should be detected and treated as that slash command, the same as if it had been typed from the start.

## Notes
Reported as a request for better slash command detection when changing an already-typed slash command.

issues.title: Async terminal find: update_dirty_matches can leave matches out of order → debug_assert! aborts (SIGABRT)
issues.body:
## Summary
The incremental match merge in async terminal find (`BlockFindResults::update_dirty_matches`, `app/src/terminal/find/model/async_find.rs`) can produce a match list that is **not** in ascending order. In debug builds this trips the trailing `debug_assert!` and aborts the process (`SIGABRT` / "Abort trap: 6"); in release builds the assert is stripped, so the same mis-ordering silently persists and can corrupt find count / focus-traversal / highlight rendering.

## Environment
- Build: from-source `warp-oss`, `0.1.0 (20260722.050348)` (debug profile — `./script/run`)
- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon (Mac15,8)
- Code path introduced in #9618 ("[APP-4280] Async blocklist search"); async find is now on Stable (#13515)

## Crash signature
```
Exception Type:  EXC_CRASH (SIGABRT)
Termination Reason: Namespace SIGNAL, Code 6, Abort trap: 6
Application Specific Information: abort() called

Thread 0 Crashed (main):
  core::panicking::panic_fmt
  warp::terminal::find::model::async_find::BlockFindResults::update_dirty_matches + 904
  warp::terminal::find::model::async_find::AsyncFindController::process_message
  ...::spawn_result_and_throttle_streams
  warpui_core::core::app::AppContext::relay_task_output
```
`panic_fmt` (a *formatted* panic) points at the only formatted panic in that function — the ascending-order `debug_assert!`.

## Root cause
`update_dirty_matches` picks the splice window (`replace_start` / `replace_end`) from **row** overlap between the existing matches and the dirty row range:

```rust
let replace_start = matches.iter().position(|m| m.end_row()   >= *dirty_range.start()).unwrap_or(matches.len());
let replace_end   = matches.iter().rposition(|m| m.start_row() <= *dirty_range.end()).map(|p| p + 1).unwrap_or(replace_start);
```

But `AbsoluteMatch`'s `Ord` sorts by the full **end point then start point** (row *and* column):

```rust
self.end.cmp(&other.end).then(self.start.cmp(&other.start))
```

When a block has matches sharing a row, or a match that spans rows across the dirty-range boundary, the row-based splice can insert new matches next to a retained neighbor that sorts *before* them by column — leaving the vector out of order under the real `Ord`, which the trailing assertion then rejects. (The code even documents the fragile "matches within a single grid do not overlap" assumption it relies on.)

## Reproduction (unit-level)
Existing matches (sorted): one ending on row 9, one on row 11 ending at column 2. Rescanning dirty row 10 yields a match starting on row 10 and spanning onto row 11 ending at column 4:

```
existing = [ (r9,c0)-(r9,c5), (r11,c0)-(r11,c2) ]
dirty    = 10..=10
new      = [ (r10,c0)-(r11,c4) ]   // spans the boundary row, later end column
```

The row-based splice yields `[ r9, span(end r11,c4), r11(end r11,c2) ]` → `span.end (11,4) > r11.end (11,2)` → not ascending → `debug_assert!` fires → abort.

In practice it surfaces when **Find is active on a terminal block whose content is still changing** (streaming output / scrollback churn), so `update_dirty_matches` runs repeatedly on updating dirty ranges.

## Impact
- Debug / from-source builds: hard crash (`SIGABRT`) whenever the invariant is violated.
- Release / Stable builds: no crash, but matches can be mis-ordered, affecting match count, next/previous traversal, and highlight placement.

## Suggested fix
Restore the ascending invariant after the splice (cheap `is_sorted` fast-path; re-sort only when the seam actually broke), instead of asserting it:

```rust
matches.splice(replace_range, new_matches);
if !matches.is_sorted() {
    matches.sort_unstable();
}
```

Per-block match counts are bounded and updates are throttled, so the occasional re-sort is negligible. A regression test covering the boundary-spanning case is included. A PR with the fix + test is ready.

prs.author: hkwan16
prs.title: Fix async find crash and duplicate matches while a block streams output
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #14231.

If Find is open while a block is still producing output, async find's per-block match list can end up unsorted and full of duplicates. Debug builds then abort on the `debug_assert!` in `BlockFindResults::update_dirty_matches` ("Matches should be in ascending order after update_dirty_matches"). Release builds don't crash, but the match count is inflated and next/previous and highlights are wrong.

The issue blames the row-based splice for mishandling matches that span rows at the seam. I reproduced the crash in the app with an instrumented debug build, and the splice is fine, because `find_in_range` keeps every match inside the scanned rows. The splice stays ordered as long as its inputs are correct. The inputs were wrong in two ways.

**1. A full rescan racing in-flight dirty-range results.** `invalidate_block(None)` clears the block's matches and queues a full rescan. Dirty-range results that were already in flight then land in the empty list. The full rescan's chunks are appended after them with a blind `extend`, starting again at row 0. Logged sequence from a crashing run:

```
invalidate full=true                              <- block's matches cleared, full rescan queued
dirty-result dirty=7117..=7523   existing=0       <- in-flight dirty results land after the clear
dirty-result dirty=7524..=8195   existing=1056
full-chunk   rows 0..999          existing=2855    <- full scan appended from row 0 after row 8195
...
dirty-result dirty=8195..=8747   existing=26051   <- list is unsorted (row 8194 then row 0) -> assert
```

Fix: Full-scan and dirty-range chunks now send the same message, `BlockGridMatches`, which carries the absolute row range it scanned, and one handler merges every chunk with the replace-overlap logic in `update_dirty_matches`. Empty chunks are sent too, so they clear stale matches in their rows. The background task processes work items one at a time, so results arrive in scan order and the latest result for a row range wins.

**2. Scrollback truncation shifting rows between enqueue and scan.** On master, dirty work items store grid-relative rows plus the truncation count at enqueue time. Under heavy output, thousands of lines can be truncated before the item is scanned, so the scan reads rows that have shifted. The batch is also labeled with the stale count, while each `AbsoluteMatch` uses the current one. In one logged run, a batch labeled `48331..=49330` had its matches at rows `53934..=54933`. Separately, once a grid is at its scroll limit the cursor stays on the same grid row while lines are truncated, so grid-relative find-dirty tracking also misses rows that were written.

Fix: Track positions in absolute rows end to end. `GridHandler` records find-dirty rows as absolute rows (`take_find_dirty_rows_range` now returns `RangeInclusive<u64>`), work items carry that range with no truncation count, and `scan_grid_chunked` walks an absolute cursor. Each chunk is mapped to grid rows by `next_chunk_rows` under the same lock as the scan, skipping rows already truncated, so a chunk's stated range always covers exactly the rows scanned.

The `debug_assert!` is unchanged. I didn't re-sort or dedupe after the splice, because that would hide the crash and leave release builds with duplicate matches and wrong counts.

Notes for reviewers:
- `DirtyRangeMatches` is gone. The single handler records the block's `TotalIndex`, merges, prunes truncated matches, auto-selects the first match and recomputes filtering for every chunk. This also fixes a gap on master where matches that only ever arrived through dirty ranges were counted but couldn't be focused, because the dirty path never recorded the block's `TotalIndex`.
- An empty chunk that overlaps no stored matches skips the merge and the focus rebuild, so rare queries over many blocks don't pay that cost for each empty chunk. If the block has no stored matches at all, it returns without taking the terminal model lock. If it does, it first prunes matches truncated from scrollback and refreshes the count and focus if any were removed.
- `GridHandler::take_find_dirty_rows_range` changes from `usize` grid rows to `u64` absolute rows. The only callers are in `app/src/terminal/find`. I removed `find_dirty_rows_range`, which had no callers.
- Possible follow-ups (not in this PR):
  - The streaming path in `TerminalFindModel` requests a full rescan whenever no output rows are dirty. That's what triggers the race, and it probably costs performance on large blocks too.
  - A match soft-wrapped across a scan batch boundary isn't found, since each batch is bounded to its rows. This predates this change and makes the final count vary by about 1 between identical runs.

### Describe the bug

Warp speaks the kitty keyboard protocol, but with `REPORT_ALTERNATE_KEYS` (flag 4) enabled it never sends the base layout key, the third sub-field of the key code. On a layout with no Latin letters (Russian, Ukrainian, Greek, Hebrew) that field is the only thing an application has to match a chord against, because the primary key code there is the layout's own codepoint. So Ctrl+V just disappears.

Russian layout, Ctrl+V, what Warp actually sends:

```
CSI 1084 ; 5 u        (1084 = U+043C, Cyrillic "m", the letter printed on that key)

```

What the protocol asks for:

```
CSI 1084 : : 118 ; 5 u    (118 = "v", the PC-101 key at that physical position)

```

I went digging in `crates/warp_terminal/src/model/escape_sequences/kitty_keyboard_protocol.rs`. The key-part builder documents its format as `unicode-key-code[:shifted-key]`, and it only ever emits the shifted key, only while Shift is held. There is no third sub-field anywhere in that file, so half of flag 4 is simply missing.

Where this bites: Claude Code turns the protocol on in Warp (it sends `CSI <u`, `CSI >5u`, `CSI >4;2m`) and binds image paste to Ctrl+V. Its parser already handles the fallback, it reads the third sub-field when Ctrl is held and the primary key code is non-ASCII, so the chord would start working the moment Warp fills the field in. Right now pasting an image into Claude Code does nothing at all while a Cyrillic layout is active. The same keypress works in Terminal.app, which does not implement the kitty protocol and just sends the legacy 0x16 control byte.

I have opened #15647 as a draft with the fix and tests

### To reproduce

1.  Switch the input source to Russian (any Cyrillic layout will do).
2.  Run this in Warp. It enables the same flags Claude Code enables, then dumps the raw bytes:

```sh
python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys, tty, termios
fd = sys.stdin.fileno()
old = termios.tcgetattr(fd)
try:
    tty.setraw(fd)
    sys.stdout.write("\x1b[<u\x1b[>5u")   # kitty keyboard protocol, flags 1 + 4
    sys.stdout.flush()
    print("press ctrl+v now\r")
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.raw.read(32)
finally:
    sys.stdout.write("\x1b[<u")
    termios.tcsetattr(fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, old)
print("\r\nreceived:", data)
EOF

```

3.  Press Ctrl+V.

Got:

```
received: b'\x1b[1084;5u'

```

Wanted:

```
received: b'\x1b[1084::118;5u'

```

On a US layout the same script prints `b'\x1b[118;5u'`, which is fine, there the key code is already the Latin letter.

When I have Russian layout set, Ctrl+V in Claude Code opened in Warp, should paste an image from the clipboard

On layouts with no Latin letters the key code is the layout's own codepoint, so there's nothing to match a chord against. Ctrl+V on Russian arrived as `CSI 1084 ; 5 u` (1084 is U+043C) and got silently dropped. Now it's `CSI 1084 : : 118 ; 5 u`, 118 being `v` at that physical position on PC-101.

`KeyCode::base_layout_key()` in warpui_core's `platform/keyboard.rs` does the mapping, macOS fills it in `mac/event.rs` from `scancode_to_physicalkey`, `keystroke_to_csi_u` emits it. It's omitted when it equals the key code, so Latin layouts are byte-identical to before. winit and crossterm pass `None` (`us_qwerty_fallback_for_chord` there returns the shifted symbol for punctuation, so it isn't reusable).

Fixes #15646

-   `crates/warpui_core/src/platform/keyboard_tests.rs`: the mapping returns the US-layout character for character keys and `None` for keys that produce none.
-   `test_keyboard_enhancement_base_layout_key` in `crates/warp_terminal/src/model/escape_sequences_tests.rs` covers the Cyrillic case, the US-layout case where the field gets omitted, and the case where flag 4 is off.

Manual testing was on macOS 26.6.2 (25G83, Apple Silicon) with the Russian input source active, running the branch build through `./script/run`. This script turns on exactly the flags Claude Code enables in Warp and prints the raw bytes of one key press:

```python
import sys, tty, termios

old = termios.tcgetattr(fd)
try:
    tty.setraw(fd)
    sys.stdout.write("\x1b[<u\x1b[>5u")
    sys.stdout.flush()
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.raw.read(32)
finally:
    sys.stdout.write("\x1b[<u")
    termios.tcsetattr(fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, old)
print("\r\nreceived:", data)

```

Ctrl+V, before and after:

```
Warp 0.2026.07.01.09.21.01:   received: b'\x1b[1084;5u'
this branch via ./script/run: received: b'\x1b[1084::118;5u'

```

On a US layout both builds print `b'\x1b[118;5u'`, unchanged.

issues.body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there

### Describe the bug

Hermes (Nous Research) is already a recognized `CLIAgent` — command prefix `hermes`, display name, brand color, and skill providers are all registered in `app/src/terminal/cli_agent.rs`. But structured OSC 777 notifications titled `warp://cli-agent` with `"agent":"hermes"` are silently dropped: `is_agent_supported()` returns `false` because `create_handler()` in `app/src/terminal/cli_agent_sessions/listener/mod.rs` has no arm for `CLIAgent::Hermes`.

As a result, Hermes sessions get none of the rich-status UI that Droid / Pi / OhMyPi / Auggie get from the same protocol: no tab status badges and no notification mailbox entries.

### To reproduce

1. In any Warp tab, emit a structured CLI agent event pair:

```sh
printf '\033]777;notify;warp://cli-agent;{"v":1,"agent":"hermes","event":"prompt_submit","session_id":"s1","query":"test"}\007'
printf '\033]777;notify;warp://cli-agent;{"v":1,"agent":"hermes","event":"stop","session_id":"s1"}\007'
```

2. Check the notification mailbox (bell icon) and the tab strip.

Observed: nothing — no mailbox entry, no badge. The identical payloads with `"agent":"droid"` immediately produce a "Task completed" mailbox entry.

### Expected behavior

Hermes events flow through `DefaultSessionListener` like Droid/Pi/Auggie — Hermes needs no special event filtering, and user-configured hooks (e.g. the community [warp-hermes](https://github.com/DarkGenius/warp-hermes) hook set) or future integrations can emit the standard protocol today.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64)

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9 (arm64-apple-darwin25.0)

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.08.26.17.59.stable_01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes — the `warp://cli-agent` OSC 777 protocol is Warp-specific.

### Additional context

Proposed fix: PR #15665 (adds `CLIAgent::Hermes` to the `DefaultSessionListener` arm of `create_handler`, plus tests).
